turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
I'm not upset, Hale. I'm asking a question. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
But I'm not changing the grade.
Then on what basis? Your own procedure says a parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Owen found out from his phone in the middle of class.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.
Refusing isn't a reason. So far you've given me a zero and no document, and the one rule I can read says you called me first. If there's something behind it, put it on the table.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.
Then I'll have it in your words. Email me tonight that you entered the zero without calling me and won't withdraw it, and I'll take that to the principal in the morning.
